_why: The generator's source, @nwpr/airport-codes, wraps the OpenFlights database,
which stopped being meaningfully updated around 2017. That is old enough to
matter: Berlin Brandenburg opened in 2020 and is absent, while the three
Berlin airports it replaced are all still listed. Someone planning a flight
to Berlin was offered a choice of three closed airports and not the open one.
These corrections are applied at generation time. Each carries the date the
change happened so the next person can tell a deliberate fix from a typo.
Removing a closed airport does cost something — a historic trip that used it
loses its distance and timezone — but the statistics report unmeasured legs
rather than hiding them, and a planner offering a runway that is now a park

add.name: Berlin Brandenburg Airport
add.note: Opened 31 October 2020; replaced TXL and SXF.

remove.note: Berlin Schoenefeld — became BER Terminal 5, no longer a separate airport.
Berlin Tempelhof — closed 30 October 2008, now a public park.
Beijing Nanyuan — closed 25 September 2019, traffic moved to PKX.
